# Overview

This document covers the first half of the pipeline: loading the two
MASST exports, selecting datasets with both compounds, tiering them by
study-design suitability, picking one prototype, and running the full
single-dataset analysis (EIC extraction, peak detection, and
parent/metabolite ratio statistics).

Part 2 (`all-datasets-analysis.qmd`) scales the same analysis to all
Tier-B datasets.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-part1
%%| fig-cap: "Part 1 pipeline — from search results to single-dataset ratio statistics."
flowchart LR
  A["Search results\n2 compound files"] --> B["Shared datasets\n26 found"]
  B --> C["Summary table\npick prototype manually"]
  C --> D["Access raw spectra\nno full download"]
  D --> E["Verify compound\nidentity"]
  E --> F["Extract signal\nboth compounds"]
  F --> G["Detect peaks · join samples\nparent / metabolite ratio"]
```

## why Omeprazol
Omeprazole is widely used for CYP2C19 phenotyping. When administered as a
 racemic mixture, (R-S)-omeprazole undergoes stereoselective metabolism and
 is primarily metabolized to (R)-5-hydroxyomeprazole via CYP2C19/CYP3A and
 (S)-5-hydroxyomeprazole via CYP2C19. Cytochrome P450 2C19 (CYP2C19) enzyme is estimated to metabolize approximately 15% of all marketed drugs, among which proton pump inhibitors, antiplatelet agents, antidepressants, beta-blockers, benzodiazepines and many other compounds
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/bcpt.14095

could also add a second probe pair (e.g., dextromethorphan/dextrorphan for CYP2D6. to show that it can be applied ot others.

title such as: Quantitative post-MASST reverse metabolomics enables pharmacoepidemiology of CYP2C19 activity across public repositories

# Setup

```{r setup}
library(Spectra)
library(MsBackendMassIVE)
library(xcms)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

library(RuSirius)
```

# Compound pair

| role | compound | formula | monoisotopic mass | InChIKey block 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent | omeprazole | C17H19N3O3S | 345.1147 | SUBDBMMJDZJVOS |
| metabolite | 5-hydroxyomeprazole | C17H19N3O4S | 361.1096 | CMZHQFXXAAIBKE |

The parent/5-OH ratio is a classical CYP2C19 phenotyping readout.
Both compounds are queried in positive and negative mode; downstream
code picks the adduct with the most hits per dataset and collapses
adducts so each compound is a single feature per sample.

```{r compound-spec}
compound_spec <- data.frame(
  role    = c("parent",       "metabolite"),
  name    = c("omeprazole",   "5-hydroxyomeprazole"),
  formula = c("C17H19N3O3S",  "C17H19N3O4S"),
  mz_pos  = c(346.1220,       362.1169)   # [M+H]+, are these rigth
)
```

# MASST exports

Two StructureMASST queries on GNPS2 with identical settings
(cosine ≥ 0.7, matched peaks ≥ 3, analog search off, both polarities).

| compound | GNPS2 session |
|---|---|
| omeprazole | `2399487d18d6` |
| 5-hydroxyomeprazole | `4c9e1b910599` |

```{r load-hits}
read_masst <- function(path, role) {
  x <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
  x[x == "missing value"] <- NA
  parts        <- strsplit(x$USI, ":", fixed = TRUE)
  x$file_path  <- vapply(parts, `[`, character(1), 3)
  x$scan_str   <- vapply(parts, \(p) p[length(p)], character(1))  # keep as character
  x$role       <- role
  x
}

all_hits <- rbind(
  read_masst("Omeoprazole.csv",          "parent"),
  read_masst("5-hydroxyomeprazole.csv",  "metabolite")
)
```

## Remove corrupted USIs

Some USIs carry the scan number `4294967295` — the maximum value of a
32-bit unsigned integer. This value is written by certain mzML converters when
the scan index is missing or could not be resolved. We remove them as they
cannot give us the position of the spectrum of interest in the raw file.

```{r filter-corrupt-usi}
INVALID_SCAN_STR <- "4294967295"

n_corrupt <- sum(all_hits$scan_str == INVALID_SCAN_STR, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Corrupted USIs removed:", n_corrupt,
    "(", round(100 * n_corrupt / nrow(all_hits), 1), "% of all hits)\n")

all_hits           <- all_hits[all_hits$scan_str != INVALID_SCAN_STR, ]
all_hits$scan_id   <- as.integer(all_hits$scan_str)   # now safe to convert
all_hits$scan_str  <- NULL                             # drop the staging column
```

## Infer adduct from observed precursor m/z

MASST reports an `Adduct` column, but it's inherited from whichever library
spectrum matched and does not always reflect how *our* compound ionised in
the query data. We know the target formula per role, so for each hit we
compute the theoretical m/z of a set of common adducts and pick the one
closest to the observed `Precursor_MZ` within a ppm tolerance. This
ground-truthed adduct is what we feed to SIRIUS later.

```{r infer-adduct}
library(MetaboCoreUtils)

ADDUCT_CANDIDATES <- c(
  "[M+H]+", "[M+Na]+", "[M+K]+", "[M+NH4]+",
  "[M-H]-", "[M+Cl]-"
)

infer_adduct <- function(obs_mz, formula, ppm = 20,
                         candidates = ADDUCT_CANDIDATES) {
  if (is.na(obs_mz) || is.na(formula)) return(NA_character_)
  mass <- calculateMass(formula)
  theo <- vapply(candidates, function(a) mass2mz(mass, adduct = a)[[1]],
                 numeric(1))
  diff_ppm <- abs(obs_mz - theo) / theo * 1e6
  best <- which.min(diff_ppm)
  if (diff_ppm[best] > ppm) NA_character_ else candidates[best]
}

role_formula <- setNames(compound_spec$formula, compound_spec$role)

all_hits$adduct_inferred <- mapply(
  infer_adduct,
  all_hits$Precursor_MZ,
  role_formula[all_hits$role],
  USE.NAMES = FALSE
)

# Coverage and adduct breakdown per role
table(role   = all_hits$role,
      adduct = all_hits$adduct_inferred,
      useNA  = "ifany")
```

# Dataset selection

## D_both — datasets where both compounds appear

```{r d-both}
D_parent     <- unique(all_hits$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession[all_hits$role == "parent"])
D_metabolite <- unique(all_hits$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession[all_hits$role == "metabolite"])
D_both       <- intersect(D_parent, D_metabolite)

cat("parent:", length(D_parent), "| metabolite:", length(D_metabolite),
    "| both:", length(D_both), "\n")
```

Pre-computed: 53 parent datasets, 30 metabolite datasets, **26 in both**
(26/30 metabolite datasets also contain the parent — high co-occurrence).

## Initial screening

13 of the 26 D_both datasets were excluded at initial inspection before
detailed curation. Two exclusion categories:

* **DIA/SWATH** — acquisition mode incompatible with single-scan MASST matching
* **no_metadata** — no sample-level metadata available in the public deposit

```{r initial-screening}
EXCLUDE_INITIAL <- c(
  MSV000085870 = "DIA/SWATH",
  MSV000091520 = "DIA/SWATH",
  MSV000093072 = "DIA/SWATH",
  MSV000094395 = "DIA/SWATH",
  MSV000094515 = "DIA/SWATH",
  MSV000095726 = "no_metadata",
  MSV000096359 = "no_metadata",
  MSV000096884 = "no_metadata",
  MSV000097110 = "no_metadata",
  MSV000097935 = "no_metadata",
  MTBLS12231   = "no_metadata",
  MTBLS12372   = "no_metadata",
  MTBLS417     = "no_metadata"
)

dataset_overlap <- all_hits[
  all_hits$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession %in% D_both &
  !all_hits$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession %in% names(EXCLUDE_INITIAL), ]

cat("After initial screening:", length(unique(dataset_overlap$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession)),
    "datasets\n")
```

## Manual dataset curation
T
Remaining datasets were reviewed individually. Decisions are recorded in
`dataset_curation_table.csv` (`keep_for_ratio` column). Two further
exclusion categories apply here:

* **In vitro / artefact** — MASST hits arise from compound-spiked experiments,
  not biological patient exposure.
* **Insufficient metadata** — phenotype data is in the publication supplementary
  only and cannot be linked to file names without additional manual work.

```{r manual-curation}
curation <- read.csv("dataset_curation_table.csv", check.names = FALSE)
curation[, c("dataset_id", "keep_for_ratio", "reason")]
```

```{r apply-curation}
keep_ids   <- curation$dataset_id[curation$keep_for_ratio == TRUE]
before_ids <- unique(dataset_overlap$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession)

hits_curated <- dataset_overlap[
  dataset_overlap$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession %in% keep_ids, ]

removed <- setdiff(before_ids, keep_ids)
cat("Datasets kept   :", length(unique(hits_curated$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession)), "\n")
cat("Datasets removed:", length(removed), "\n")
cat(paste(" ", removed, "<-",
          curation$reason[match(removed, curation$dataset_id)],
          collapse = "\n"), "\n")

write.csv(hits_curated, "hits_curated.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# MASST hits confirmation

SIRIUS confirmation is run in three separate notebooks, one per repository:

* `masst-hit-confirmation.qmd` → `hits-confirmed-massive.csv`
* `metaboLights-confirmation.qmd` → `hits-confirmed-metaboLights.csv`
* `metabolomics-workbench-confirmation.qmd` → `hits-confirmed-metabolomics-workbench.csv`

## Load and combine

Each file is filtered to its own accession prefix before combining to
avoid cross-contamination (the `resolve_all` helper reads the whole
`results/` folder regardless of which notebook called it).

```{r load-confirmed}
conf_massive <- read.csv("hits-confirmed-massive.csv",    check.names = FALSE)
conf_mtbls   <- read.csv("hits-confirmed-metaboLights.csv", check.names = FALSE)
conf_mwb     <- read.csv("hits-confirmed-metabolomics-workbench.csv", check.names = FALSE)

conf_massive <- conf_massive[startsWith(conf_massive$dataset_id, "MSV"),  ]
conf_mtbls   <- conf_mtbls  [startsWith(conf_mtbls$dataset_id,   "MTBLS"),]
conf_mwb     <- conf_mwb    [startsWith(conf_mwb$dataset_id,     "ST"),   ]

conf_all <- rbind(conf_massive, conf_mtbls, conf_mwb)

# Ensure all expected columns exist (older confirmed CSVs lack mz/adduct_inferred)
for (col in c("mz", "adduct_inferred", "source_file")) {
  if (!col %in% names(conf_all)) conf_all[[col]] <- NA
}

# Patch rt / mz / adduct_inferred / source_file from per-dataset hits_rt.csv.
# source_file is always re-patched (it is never written to the confirmed CSV
# itself, so it is always NA there regardless of whether rt/mz are present).
need_patch_ds <- unique(conf_all$dataset_id[
  is.na(conf_all$rt) | is.na(conf_all$mz) |
  is.na(conf_all$adduct_inferred) | is.na(conf_all$source_file)
])
if (length(need_patch_ds)) {
  cat("Patching rt/mz/adduct from hits_rt.csv for",
      length(need_patch_ds), "dataset(s):\n")
  for (ds in need_patch_ds) {
    rt_path <- file.path("results", ds, "hits_rt.csv")
    if (!file.exists(rt_path)) {
      cat("  [", ds, "] no hits_rt.csv — skipped\n"); next
    }
    rt_map <- read.csv(rt_path, check.names = FALSE)
    idx    <- conf_all$dataset_id == ds
    keys_l <- paste(conf_all$role[idx], conf_all$xcms_fts[idx])
    keys_r <- paste(rt_map$role,         rt_map$xcms_fts)
    m      <- match(keys_l, keys_r)
    if (is.null(conf_all$rt[idx]) || any(is.na(conf_all$rt[idx])))
      conf_all$rt[idx] <- ifelse(is.na(conf_all$rt[idx]),
                                  rt_map$rt[m], conf_all$rt[idx])
    if ("mz" %in% names(rt_map))
      conf_all$mz[idx] <- ifelse(is.na(conf_all$mz[idx]),
                                  rt_map$mz[m], conf_all$mz[idx])
    if ("adduct_inferred" %in% names(rt_map))
      conf_all$adduct_inferred[idx] <- ifelse(
        is.na(conf_all$adduct_inferred[idx]),
        rt_map$adduct_inferred[m], conf_all$adduct_inferred[idx])
    if ("file" %in% names(rt_map))
      conf_all$source_file[idx] <- ifelse(
        is.na(conf_all$source_file[idx]),
        rt_map$file[m], conf_all$source_file[idx])
    cat("  [", ds, "] patched (non-NA mz:",
        sum(!is.na(conf_all$mz[idx])), "/", sum(idx),
        ", non-NA adduct_inferred:",
        sum(!is.na(conf_all$adduct_inferred[idx])), "/", sum(idx), ")\n")
  }
}

conf_all$confidence <- factor(conf_all$confidence,
                               levels = c("strict", "standard", "liberal",
                                          "not_confirmed"))

# Join chromatography type from curation table
# (curation was loaded in the manual-curation chunk above)
if (!exists("curation"))
  curation <- read.csv("dataset_curation_table.csv", check.names = FALSE)
curation$chrom_type <- dplyr::case_when(
  grepl("HILIC|ZIC|pHILIC", curation$chromatography, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "HILIC",
  grepl("RP|C18|reverse", curation$chromatography, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "RP",
  TRUE                                                                     ~ "Unknown"
)
conf_all <- dplyr::left_join(
  conf_all,
  curation[, c("dataset_id", "chrom_type")],
  by = "dataset_id"
)

cat("Total confirmed features:", nrow(conf_all), "\n")
cat("Datasets             :", length(unique(conf_all$dataset_id)), "\n")
cat("Chromatography types :\n")
print(table(unique(conf_all[, c("dataset_id", "chrom_type")])$chrom_type))
```

## Resolve assay per confirmed feature

Multi-assay studies (mostly MetaboLights, sometimes Metabolomics Workbench)
host several assays per dataset — different polarities, columns, or
matrices. Confirmed features from different assays must NEVER be mixed:
they map to different chromatography and ionisation chemistry, and
therefore to different RT and m/z windows. We resolve the assay for each
confirmed feature from its `source_file` (the MS file where SIRIUS matched
the compound) and store the result in a new `assay` column. Every
downstream filter, RT/mz summary, and EIC extraction then groups by
(`dataset_id`, `assay`) so multi-assay studies stay separated.

```{r resolve-assay}
META_DIR <- "dataset_metadata"

# --- MetaboLights ---------------------------------------------------------
# Build basename(file) → assay_file_name lookup by scanning every
# a_{ds}_*.txt assay table cached in dataset_metadata/.
mtbls_assay_lookup <- function(ds) {
  fs <- list.files(META_DIR, pattern = paste0("^a_", ds, "_.*\\.txt$"),
                   full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(fs)) return(character(0))
  out <- character(0)
  for (fp in fs) {
    adf <- tryCatch(read.delim(fp, check.names = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(adf)) next
    file_cols <- grep("Spectral Data File", names(adf),
                      value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
    files <- unlist(lapply(file_cols, function(c) adf[[c]]), use.names = FALSE)
    files <- basename(trimws(files))
    files <- files[!is.na(files) & nchar(files) > 0]
    if (!length(files)) next
    out <- c(out, setNames(rep(basename(fp), length(files)), files))
  }
  out
}

# --- Metabolomics Workbench -----------------------------------------------
# Build per-feature AN assignment. RAW_FILE_NAME is shared across AN files
# (SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS is identical), so we disambiguate by ION_MODE
# matched against the confirmed adduct polarity, then narrow by filename
# polarity tokens when several AN files match the same mode.
mwb_assay_for_rows <- function(ds, conf_rows) {
  fs <- list.files(META_DIR, pattern = paste0("^", ds, "_AN.*\\.txt$"),
                   full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(fs)) return(rep(NA_character_, nrow(conf_rows)))
  an_pol <- vapply(fs, function(fp) {
    ln <- readLines(fp, warn = FALSE)
    trimws(sub("^MS:ION_MODE\\s+", "",
               grep("^MS:ION_MODE", ln, value = TRUE)[1]))
  }, character(1))
  out <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(conf_rows))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(conf_rows))) {
    adu <- conf_rows$adduct_inferred[i]
    if (is.na(adu)) next
    pol <- if (endsWith(trimws(adu), "+")) "positive" else "negative"
    candidates <- fs[grepl(pol, an_pol, ignore.case = TRUE)]
    if (!length(candidates)) next
    sf <- basename(conf_rows$source_file[i])
    if (length(candidates) > 1 && !is.na(sf) && nchar(sf)) {
      hit <- vapply(candidates, function(fp) {
        any(grepl(sf, readLines(fp, warn = FALSE), fixed = TRUE))
      }, logical(1))
      if (any(hit)) candidates <- candidates[hit]
    }
    out[i] <- basename(candidates[1])
  }
  out
}

conf_all$assay <- NA_character_

# MassIVE: a single metadata file per dataset → assay collapsed to dataset_id
msv_idx <- startsWith(conf_all$dataset_id, "MSV")
conf_all$assay[msv_idx] <- conf_all$dataset_id[msv_idx]

# MetaboLights: lookup per source_file basename
for (ds in unique(conf_all$dataset_id[startsWith(conf_all$dataset_id, "MTBLS")])) {
  lookup <- mtbls_assay_lookup(ds)
  idx    <- conf_all$dataset_id == ds
  src    <- basename(conf_all$source_file[idx])
  conf_all$assay[idx] <- unname(lookup[src])
}

# Metabolomics Workbench: polarity-based AN selection
for (ds in unique(conf_all$dataset_id[startsWith(conf_all$dataset_id, "ST")])) {
  idx <- conf_all$dataset_id == ds
  conf_all$assay[idx] <- mwb_assay_for_rows(ds, conf_all[idx, , drop = FALSE])
}

cat("Assay resolved for", sum(!is.na(conf_all$assay)), "/", nrow(conf_all),
    "confirmed features\n")
print(table(dataset_id = conf_all$dataset_id, assay = conf_all$assay,
            useNA = "ifany"))

# Datasets where more than one assay carries confirmed features
ma_ds <- vapply(split(conf_all$assay, conf_all$dataset_id),
                function(x) length(unique(na.omit(x))) > 1, logical(1))
multi_assay_ds <- names(ma_ds)[ma_ds]
if (length(multi_assay_ds))
  cat("Multi-assay datasets (kept separate downstream):\n  ",
      paste(multi_assay_ds, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Adduct consistency rule

For the parent/metabolite ratio to be interpretable, both compounds must
be extracted using the **same adduct** (same ionisation chemistry, same
nominal m/z offset). A dataset where omeprazole is confirmed as [M+H]+
but 5-OH-omeprazole only as [M+Na]+ is not a problem per se — both
adducts are real — but the EIC windows will target different m/z values
and mixing them in the ratio is confusing.

**Decision rule:** we restrict all diagnostic plots and downstream EIC
windows to adducts that are observed in **both** parent and metabolite
confirmed features. Adducts that appear in only one role are dropped.
This does not discard entire datasets; it only drops individual features
whose adduct was not replicated on the other side of the ratio.

```{r shared-adducts}
adducts_parent <- unique(conf_all$adduct_inferred[
  conf_all$role == "parent" & !is.na(conf_all$adduct_inferred)])
adducts_metab  <- unique(conf_all$adduct_inferred[
  conf_all$role == "metabolite" & !is.na(conf_all$adduct_inferred)])
shared_adducts <- intersect(adducts_parent, adducts_metab)

cat("Adducts in parent    :", paste(adducts_parent, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Adducts in metabolite:", paste(adducts_metab,  collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Shared adducts kept  :", paste(shared_adducts, collapse = ", "), "\n")

conf_all_shared <- conf_all[
  !is.na(conf_all$adduct_inferred) &
  conf_all$adduct_inferred %in% shared_adducts, ]
cat("Features retained:", nrow(conf_all_shared), "of", nrow(conf_all), "\n")
```

## RT across datasets

Retention times vary widely between datasets because each study used a
different LC gradient. This is expected and will be resolved by
per-dataset RT windows in the EIC step. What matters here is
**within-dataset consistency**: features of the same compound in the
same dataset should cluster tightly.

Note: only adducts present in both parent and metabolite are displayed
(see adduct consistency rule above).

```{r plot-rt-discrepancy, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
CONFIDENCE_COLOURS <- c(strict = "#1A7837", standard = "#74C476",
                         liberal = "#FEC44F", not_confirmed = "#D7191C")

conf_all_shared |>
  filter(!is.na(rt)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dataset_id, y = rt,
             colour = confidence, shape = adduct_inferred)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 2.5, width = 0.15, alpha = 0.85) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.5,
               linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(chrom_type ~ role, scales = "free", space = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = CONFIDENCE_COLOURS, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_discrete(drop = TRUE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Retention time (s)",
       colour = "Confidence", shape = "Adduct",
       title = "RT of confirmed features — cross-dataset comparison") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"))
```

## m/z deviation across datasets

The observed precursor m/z (from the actual MS2 scan in the raw file)
should match the theoretical m/z of the inferred adduct within the
instrument's mass accuracy. We compute deviation in ppm:
`(observed − theoretical) / theoretical × 10⁶`.

A well-calibrated Orbitrap is typically within ±5 ppm; anything above
±10 ppm suggests either a calibration issue in that dataset or a
mis-assigned adduct. The ±5 ppm dashed lines serve as a visual guide.
This plot is also used to sanity-check whether our adduct inference
(from `MetaboCoreUtils::infer_adduct`) is consistent with what SIRIUS
independently resolved in the `adduct` column of the confirmed CSV.

```{r mz-deviation, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
library(MetaboCoreUtils)

role_formula <- setNames(compound_spec$formula, compound_spec$role)

conf_all_shared$mz_theo <- mapply(
  function(f, a) {
    if (is.na(f) || is.na(a)) return(NA_real_)
    mass2mz(calculateMass(f), adduct = a)[[1]]
  },
  role_formula[conf_all_shared$role],
  conf_all_shared$adduct_inferred,
  USE.NAMES = FALSE
)
conf_all_shared$mz_ppm_dev <- (conf_all_shared$mz - conf_all_shared$mz_theo) /
                               conf_all_shared$mz_theo * 1e6

# Also propagate to conf_all for use in proto-config
conf_all$mz_theo    <- conf_all_shared$mz_theo[
  match(paste(conf_all$dataset_id, conf_all$role, conf_all$xcms_fts),
        paste(conf_all_shared$dataset_id, conf_all_shared$role,
              conf_all_shared$xcms_fts))]
conf_all$mz_ppm_dev <- conf_all_shared$mz_ppm_dev[
  match(paste(conf_all$dataset_id, conf_all$role, conf_all$xcms_fts),
        paste(conf_all_shared$dataset_id, conf_all_shared$role,
              conf_all_shared$xcms_fts))]

cat("m/z deviation summary (ppm):\n")
print(summary(conf_all_shared$mz_ppm_dev))

conf_all_shared |>
  filter(!is.na(mz_ppm_dev)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dataset_id, y = mz_ppm_dev,
             colour = adduct_inferred, shape = adduct_inferred)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,        linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-5, 5), linetype = 3, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_jitter(size = 2.5, width = 0.15, alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_grid(chrom_type ~ role, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_shape_discrete(drop = TRUE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "m/z deviation (ppm)",
       colour = "Adduct", shape = "Adduct",
       title = "Precursor m/z deviation vs theoretical adduct mass",
       caption = "Dashed: 0 ppm  ·  Dotted: ±5 ppm") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"))
```

## Adduct distribution per role

```{r adduct-distribution}
table(role   = conf_all_shared$role,
      adduct = conf_all_shared$adduct_inferred,
      useNA  = "ifany")
```

## Filter: keep highest confidence level per dataset

SIRIUS can return multiple candidate structures at different confidence
tiers for the same feature. We keep only the highest tier reached per
(dataset, role) pair. For a dataset that has one strict and two standard
features for the parent, we keep only the strict one — it provides the
most reliable RT anchor and m/z for EIC extraction.

**Why this matters for the ratio:** if we kept both strict and standard
features for the same compound in a dataset, we would be double-counting
that dataset in downstream statistics. One confirmed m/z window per
compound per dataset is what we need.

```{r filter-best-confidence}
CONF_ORDER <- c(strict = 1, standard = 2, liberal = 3, not_confirmed = 4)

conf_best <- conf_all_shared |>
  group_by(dataset_id, assay, role) |>
  filter(CONF_ORDER[as.character(confidence)] ==
           min(CONF_ORDER[as.character(confidence)])) |>
  ungroup()

cat("Features after confidence filter:", nrow(conf_best), "\n")
cat("Features removed               :", nrow(conf_all_shared) - nrow(conf_best), "\n")
```

## Filter: both parent and metabolite must be confirmed

The CYP2C19 ratio requires **both** omeprazole (parent) and
5-OH-omeprazole (metabolite) to be detectable in the same dataset.
A dataset with only the parent confirmed cannot contribute a ratio — it
can tell us that omeprazole is present (consistent with PPI use) but
not how efficiently CYP2C19 is metabolising it.

Datasets confirmed for only one role are dropped here. The diagnostic
table below identifies the reason for each dropout by checking the full
SIRIUS output (including liberal and not_confirmed tiers), so we can
distinguish between "SIRIUS ran and found nothing convincing" vs "SIRIUS
never ran for this role" (e.g., no MASST hits for metabolite in that
dataset to begin with).

```{r diagnose-missing-roles}
# Read ALL SIRIUS results (not filtered to strict/standard) to see full picture
read_all_results <- function(results_dir = "results") {
  CONFIDENCE_LEVELS <- c("strict", "standard", "liberal", "not_confirmed")
  CONF_ORDER        <- c(strict = 1, standard = 2, liberal = 3, not_confirmed = 4)

  datasets <- list.dirs(results_dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = FALSE)
  rows <- lapply(datasets, function(ds) {
    lapply(c("parent", "metabolite"), function(role) {
      p <- file.path(results_dir, ds, paste0(role, "_results.csv"))
      if (!file.exists(p)) return(NULL)
      res <- read.csv(p, check.names = FALSE)
      if (!nrow(res)) return(NULL)
      # just need the best confidence reached per dataset × role
      data.frame(dataset_id = ds, role = role,
                 n_features  = length(unique(res$xcms_fts)),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
  })
  do.call(rbind, unlist(rows, recursive = FALSE))
}

all_results <- read_all_results()

# What is confirmed (strict/standard) vs what was run
role_status <- all_results |>
  left_join(
    conf_best |>
      group_by(dataset_id, role) |>
      summarise(best_conf = as.character(confidence[1]), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("dataset_id", "role")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      best_conf %in% c("strict", "standard") ~ best_conf,
      !is.na(n_features)                     ~ "ran — below threshold",
      TRUE                                   ~ "no results"
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = role,
                     values_from = c(n_features, status, best_conf))

role_status |>
  filter(startsWith(dataset_id, "MTBLS") | startsWith(dataset_id, "ST")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dataset_id)
```

```{r filter-both-roles}
# Per (dataset, assay): an assay must carry both parent and metabolite
# for its ratio to be computable. Multi-assay datasets can therefore
# survive even if only one of their assays passes both-roles.
both_roles <- conf_best |>
  group_by(dataset_id, assay) |>
  filter(all(c("parent", "metabolite") %in% role)) |>
  ungroup()

ds_keys_before <- unique(paste(conf_best$dataset_id, conf_best$assay, sep = "::"))
ds_keys_after  <- unique(paste(both_roles$dataset_id, both_roles$assay, sep = "::"))
dropped_keys   <- setdiff(ds_keys_before, ds_keys_after)
cat("Dataset×assay units with both roles confirmed:",
    length(ds_keys_after), "\n")
cat("Datasets with both roles confirmed (>=1 assay):",
    length(unique(both_roles$dataset_id)), "\n")
if (length(dropped_keys)) {
  cat("Dropped dataset×assay (one role missing strict/standard):\n",
      paste("  ", dropped_keys, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
}

conf_final <- both_roles
```

conf_final |>
  filter(!is.na(rt)) |>
  group_by(dataset_id, assay, role, chrom_type) |>
