# Biological file selection

Before any download, we derive the list of biological sample files per
confirmed dataset from local metadata alone — excluding QC injections,
blanks, pooled QC, reference standards, and instrument controls.

## Metadata format differences across repositories

The three repositories store sample-level metadata in very different
structures, and **the location of the spectral file name differs in each**:

**MassIVE (GNPS / Pan-ReDU)**
: Each dataset has a metadata TSV downloaded from Pan-ReDU (or a
custom CSV from the data submitter). Both contain a `SampleType` column
(values: `"Sample"`, `"QC"`, `"Blank"`, etc.) and a `filename` column.
*TSV (Pan-ReDU):* `filename` holds the full relative path within the
MassIVE file tree, e.g.
`peak/05092023-pos-pc18-peaklist/pos_NA_8990_NA_NA_193_G_B5.mzXML`.
*CSV (submitter-provided):* `filename` holds only the bare sample stem
without extension or subdirectory, e.g. `pos_inf_non_10124_male_67_267_R_C8`.
For the CSV case, we reconstruct the full path by extracting the
directory prefix and extension pattern from the MASST hit `file_path`
entries already present in `hits_curated` for that dataset.

**MetaboLights (EBI)**
: MetaboLights uses the ISA-Tab format. The study sample file
(`s_{id}.txt`) lists sample names and phenotype factors
(`Characteristics[Sample type]`) but contains **no spectral file names**.
File names live in the assay file(s) (`a_{id}_*.txt`), which map
`Sample Name` to `Raw Spectral Data File` or `Derived Spectral Data File`.
A study may have **multiple assay files** — typically one per
chromatographic mode (positive, negative) or matrix.  We use the
`MsBackendMetaboLights` helper `mtbls_assay_data()` (with an FTP fallback)
to load each assay table, then match the confirmed MASST source files
to determine which assay(s) are relevant.  When confirmed files span
more than one assay, `bio_files_per_ds[[ds]]` becomes a **named list**
(keyed by assay file name) rather than a flat character vector.

**Metabolomics Workbench**
: Data are stored in mwtab plain-text files, one per analysis
(e.g., `ST002044_AN003325.txt`). Each contains `SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS`
lines with tab-delimited fields: tag, subject ID, sample ID, factor
string, and an optional extra field that may include `RAW_FILE_NAME=...`.
We parse these lines across all analysis files for the study and again
use confirmed source files to restrict to only the analysis/analyses
that contain real data for the compounds of interest.

```{r bio-file-selection}
library(MsBackendMetaboLights)   # mtbls_assay_data(), used in fetch_assay_table()
META_DIR <- "dataset_metadata"
EXCL_ST  <- "(?i)^(blank|qc|pool|reference|standard|control|empty)"

# ── MetaboLights helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Get list of assay file names from the ISA investigation file.
# Caches the investigation file locally; returns character vector of
# assay file names like "a_MTBLS1866_LC-MS_positive.txt".
mtbls_inv_assay_names <- function(ds) {
  inv_path <- file.path(META_DIR, paste0(ds, "_i_Investigation.txt"))
  if (!file.exists(inv_path)) {
    inv_url <- paste0("https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/metabolights/",
                      "studies/public/", ds, "/i_Investigation.txt")
    inv_lines <- tryCatch(
      readLines(url(inv_url), warn = FALSE),
      error = function(e) { message("FTP unreachable: ", e$message); NULL }
    )
    if (is.null(inv_lines)) return(NULL)
    writeLines(inv_lines, inv_path)
  } else {
    inv_lines <- readLines(inv_path, warn = FALSE)
  }
  assay_line  <- inv_lines[startsWith(inv_lines, "Study Assay File Name")]
  if (!length(assay_line)) return(NULL)
  an <- trimws(unlist(strsplit(sub("^[^\t]+\t", "", assay_line[1]), "\t")))
  an[nchar(an) > 0]
}

# Fetch (or load cached) assay table for one assay of a MetaboLights study.
# Tries mtbls_assay_data() first (MsBackendMetaboLights); falls back to FTP.
fetch_assay_table <- function(ds, assay_name) {
  cache_path <- file.path(META_DIR, assay_name)
  if (file.exists(cache_path)) return(read.delim(cache_path, check.names = FALSE))
  adf <- tryCatch(
    mtbls_assay_data(ds, assay_name),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(adf)) {
    write.table(adf, cache_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
    message("  Assay file cached (mtbls_assay_data) → ", cache_path)
    return(adf)
  }
  assay_url <- paste0("https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/metabolights/",
                      "studies/public/", ds, "/", assay_name)
  adf <- tryCatch(
    read.delim(url(assay_url), check.names = FALSE),
    error = function(e) { message("FTP fetch failed for ", assay_name, ": ", e$message); NULL }
  )
  if (!is.null(adf)) {
    write.table(adf, cache_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
    message("  Assay file cached (FTP) → ", cache_path)
  }
  adf
}

# ── Main loop ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
bio_files_per_ds  <- list()   # ds → file vector, or named list per assay
bio_assays_per_ds <- list()   # ds → assay/analysis identifiers used

for (ds in unique(conf_final$dataset_id)) {
  cat("[", ds, "]\n")

  if (startsWith(ds, "MSV")) {
    # ── MassIVE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    f <- list.files(META_DIR,
                    pattern    = paste0("^", ds, "_metadata.*\\.(tsv|csv)$"),
                    full.names = TRUE)
    if (!length(f)) { cat("  no metadata file\n"); next }

    is_tsv <- grepl("\\.tsv$", f[1])
    meta   <- if (is_tsv) read.delim(f[1], check.names = FALSE)
              else        read.csv(f[1],   check.names = FALSE)

    if ("SampleType" %in% names(meta))
      meta <- meta[!grepl(EXCL_ST, meta$SampleType, perl = TRUE), ]

    if (!is_tsv) {
      # Custom CSV: filename = bare sample stem (no extension, no subdirectory).
      # Reconstruct full relative paths using the directory prefix + extension
      # pattern observed in the MASST hit file_path entries for this dataset.
      masst_paths <- unique(hits_curated$file_path[
        hits_curated$ATTRIBUTE_DatasetAccession == ds])
      dir_prefix  <- names(which.max(table(dirname(masst_paths))))
      exts        <- tools::file_ext(masst_paths)
      ext_str     <- names(which.max(table(exts[nchar(exts) > 0])))
      ext_str     <- if (nchar(ext_str) > 0) paste0(".", ext_str) else ""
      cat("  CSV metadata — reconstructing paths: dir =", dir_prefix,
          "| ext =", ext_str, "\n")
      bio_files_per_ds[[ds]] <- file.path(dir_prefix,
                                          paste0(unique(meta$filename), ext_str))
    } else {
      bio_files_per_ds[[ds]] <- unique(meta$filename)
    }
    bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]] <- basename(f[1])

  } else if (startsWith(ds, "MTBLS")) {
    # ── MetaboLights ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    s_path <- file.path(META_DIR, paste0("s_", ds, ".txt"))
    if (!file.exists(s_path)) { cat("  no sample file\n"); next }

    samples <- read.delim(s_path, check.names = FALSE)
    st_col  <- grep("sample type", names(samples), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]
    if (!is.na(st_col))
      samples <- samples[!grepl(EXCL_ST, samples[[st_col]], perl = TRUE), ]
    bio_names <- unique(samples[["Sample Name"]])

    # Get all assay names for this study from the investigation file
    assay_names <- mtbls_inv_assay_names(ds)
    if (is.null(assay_names) || !length(assay_names)) {
      cat("  could not retrieve assay list\n"); next
    }
    cat("  assay files found:", paste(assay_names, collapse = "; "), "\n")

    # Load all assay tables and extract bio file lists.
    # fcol_pick prefers "Derived Spectral Data File" over "Raw Spectral Data File"
    # because in MetaboLights the Raw column is often all-NA while Derived has paths.
    # Also filter NA explicitly — nchar(NA) returns NA not 0, so nchar(fv)>0 alone
    # would pass NA through and cause downstream unlist() to produce NA elements.
    fcol_pick <- function(adf) {
      derived <- grep("Derived Spectral Data File", names(adf),
                      value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]
      if (!is.na(derived) && any(!is.na(adf[[derived]]))) return(derived)
      grep("Raw Spectral Data File", names(adf),
           value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]
    }
    assay_bio_files <- lapply(setNames(assay_names, assay_names), function(an) {
      adf <- fetch_assay_table(ds, an)
      if (is.null(adf)) return(character(0))
      fc <- fcol_pick(adf)
      if (is.na(fc)) return(character(0))
      rows <- adf[adf[["Sample Name"]] %in% bio_names, , drop = FALSE]
      fv   <- unique(trimws(rows[[fc]]))
      fv[!is.na(fv) & nchar(fv) > 0]
    })
    assay_bio_files <- Filter(function(x) length(x) > 0, assay_bio_files)

    # Select assays that contain confirmed source files for BOTH roles.
    # Requiring both roles in the same assay guarantees the ratio is computable.
    conf_ds_mtbls <- conf_final[conf_final$dataset_id == ds & !is.na(conf_final$source_file), ]
    src_par_mtbls <- unique(conf_ds_mtbls$source_file[conf_ds_mtbls$role == "parent"])
    src_met_mtbls <- unique(conf_ds_mtbls$source_file[conf_ds_mtbls$role == "metabolite"])

    if (length(src_par_mtbls) > 0 && length(src_met_mtbls) > 0) {
      in_par <- sapply(assay_bio_files, function(fv) any(basename(fv) %in% src_par_mtbls))
      in_met <- sapply(assay_bio_files, function(fv) any(basename(fv) %in% src_met_mtbls))
      relevant_assays <- names(assay_bio_files)[in_par & in_met]
      if (!length(relevant_assays)) {
        par_ans <- names(assay_bio_files)[in_par]
        met_ans <- names(assay_bio_files)[in_met]
        cat("  WARNING: parent confirmed in [", paste(par_ans, collapse=", "),
            "] but metabolite in [", paste(met_ans, collapse=", "),
            "] — role/assay mismatch; using all assays\n")
        relevant_assays <- names(assay_bio_files)
      }
    } else if (length(c(src_par_mtbls, src_met_mtbls)) > 0) {
      # Only one role has source_file info — best effort
      conf_src_any    <- c(src_par_mtbls, src_met_mtbls)
      in_any          <- sapply(assay_bio_files, function(fv) any(basename(fv) %in% conf_src_any))
      relevant_assays <- names(assay_bio_files)[in_any]
      cat("  NOTE: only", if (length(src_par_mtbls)) "parent" else "metabolite",
          "has confirmed source_file — assay selection partial\n")
      if (!length(relevant_assays)) relevant_assays <- names(assay_bio_files)
    } else {
      relevant_assays <- names(assay_bio_files)
      cat("  NOTE: no confirmed source_file available — using all assays\n")
    }

    bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]] <- relevant_assays

    if (length(relevant_assays) == 1) {
      bio_files_per_ds[[ds]] <- assay_bio_files[[relevant_assays]]
    } else {
      # Multi-assay: store as named list; handled downstream per assay
      bio_files_per_ds[[ds]] <- assay_bio_files[relevant_assays]
      cat("  MULTI-ASSAY:", length(relevant_assays),
          "assays contain confirmed files — bio_files_per_ds[[ds]] is a named list\n")
    }

  } else if (startsWith(ds, "ST")) {
    # ── Metabolomics Workbench — mwtab format ─────────────────────────────────
    # Each AN file has SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS lines whose tag is padded with
    # spaces before the first tab — NOT a bare tag+tab. The regex fix is to
    # match on startsWith("SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS") only (no \t requirement).
    #
    # Additionally, RAW_FILE_NAME in multi-analysis studies lists ALL raw files
    # for a sample (space-separated, one per analysis). We expand these into
    # individual rows, then use confirmed adduct polarity to restrict to the
    # correct analysis.
    mwf <- list.files(META_DIR,
                      pattern    = paste0("^", ds, "_AN.*\\.txt$"),
                      full.names = TRUE)
    if (!length(mwf)) { cat("  no mwtab file\n"); next }

    # Read ION_MODE and CHROMATOGRAPHY_TYPE per analysis file
    an_ids  <- sub(".*_(AN[0-9]+)\\.txt$", "\\1", basename(mwf))
    an_meta <- setNames(lapply(mwf, function(path) {
      ln <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
      c(ion_mode   = trimws(sub("^MS:ION_MODE\\s+", "",
                    grep("^MS:ION_MODE",            ln, value = TRUE)[1])),
        chrom_type = trimws(sub("^CH:CHROMATOGRAPHY_TYPE\\s+", "",
                    grep("^CH:CHROMATOGRAPHY_TYPE", ln, value = TRUE)[1])))
    }), an_ids)
    cat("  analyses:", paste(mapply(function(id, m)
          paste0(id, "(", m["chrom_type"], "/", m["ion_mode"], ")"),
          names(an_meta), an_meta), collapse = "; "), "\n")

    # Parse SSF from the first file (lines are identical across all AN files).
    # Match by prefix only — the tag is space-padded before the tab.
    ln  <- readLines(mwf[1], warn = FALSE)
    ssf <- ln[startsWith(ln, "SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS") & !startsWith(ln, "#")]
    if (!length(ssf)) { cat("  no SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS\n"); next }

    # Fields after splitting on tab:
    #   p[1] = "SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS   " (with trailing spaces — trimmed by strsplit)
    #   p[2] = subject (often "-")
    #   p[3] = sample_id
    #   p[4] = factors
    #   p[5] = extra string (may contain "RAW_FILE_NAME=a.mzML b.mzML c.mzML ...")
    # RAW_FILE_NAME may list multiple space-separated files for multi-analysis studies.
    ssf_rows <- lapply(strsplit(ssf, "\t"), function(p) {
      raw_str <- if (length(p) >= 5)
                   regmatches(p[5], regexpr("RAW_FILE_NAME=[^\t]+", p[5]))
                 else character(0)
      raw_str   <- sub("RAW_FILE_NAME=", "", if (length(raw_str)) raw_str else "")
      raw_files <- trimws(unlist(strsplit(raw_str, "\\s+")))
      raw_files <- raw_files[nchar(raw_files) > 0]
      if (!length(raw_files)) raw_files <- NA_character_
      data.frame(sample_id = p[3], factors = p[4],
                 raw_file  = raw_files,
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
    ssf_df <- do.call(rbind, ssf_rows)
    if (is.null(ssf_df) || nrow(ssf_df) == 0L) { cat("  no SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS\n"); next }
    ssf_df <- ssf_df[!grepl(EXCL_ST, ssf_df$factors, perl = TRUE), ]

    all_bio_raw <- unique(ssf_df$raw_file[!is.na(ssf_df$raw_file)])

    # Restrict to the confirmed analysis using:
    # (a) confirmed adduct polarity → target ION_MODE
    # (b) direct filename match against confirmed source files
    conf_ds_st  <- conf_final[conf_final$dataset_id == ds, ]
    src_par_st  <- unique(conf_ds_st$source_file[conf_ds_st$role == "parent"   & !is.na(conf_ds_st$source_file)])
    src_met_st  <- unique(conf_ds_st$source_file[conf_ds_st$role == "metabolite" & !is.na(conf_ds_st$source_file)])
    conf_src_st <- c(src_par_st, src_met_st)

    if (length(conf_src_st) > 0) {
      # Step 1: determine target ion mode from confirmed adducts
      conf_adducts_st <- unique(conf_ds_st$adduct_inferred[!is.na(conf_ds_st$adduct_inferred)])
      pos_mode_st     <- any(endsWith(trimws(conf_adducts_st), "+"))
      target_mode     <- if (pos_mode_st) "positive" else "negative"

      # Step 2: find which AN files match the target ion mode
      an_with_conf <- names(an_meta)[sapply(an_meta, function(m) {
        grepl(target_mode, m["ion_mode"], ignore.case = TRUE)
      })]
      if (!length(an_with_conf)) an_with_conf <- names(an_meta)

      # Step 3: if multiple files per sample (multi-analysis), restrict by naming.
      # Exclude files whose names contain the wrong polarity token (NEG for POS mode,
      # POS for NEG mode). Files with no polarity token in their name pass through.
      excl_pol <- if (pos_mode_st) "(?i)(^|[_-])NEG([_-]|\\.[a-zA-Z])"
                  else             "(?i)(^|[_-])POS([_-]|\\.[a-zA-Z])"
      bio_raw  <- all_bio_raw[!grepl(excl_pol, basename(all_bio_raw), perl = TRUE)]

      # Step 4: if confirmed source files directly match some bio files, try to
      # narrow further by the file-name suffix pattern of those confirmed files
      # (e.g. all confirmed files end in "_POS.mzML" → keep only *_POS.mzML).
      direct <- all_bio_raw[basename(all_bio_raw) %in% conf_src_st]
      if (length(direct) > 0) {
        sfx <- unique(regmatches(basename(direct),
                                 regexpr("_[^_]+\\.[^.]+$", basename(direct))))
        if (length(sfx) == 1 && nchar(sfx) > 2) {
          pat     <- paste0(gsub("([.+*?\\[\\]()|])", "\\\\\\1", sfx), "$")
          sub_raw <- all_bio_raw[grepl(pat, basename(all_bio_raw))]
          if (length(sub_raw) > 0) {
            bio_raw <- sub_raw
            cat("  file suffix from conf_src:", sfx, "\n")
          }
        }
      }

      # Both-roles check within the selected files
      has_par_st <- length(src_par_st) == 0 || any(basename(bio_raw) %in% src_par_st)
      has_met_st <- length(src_met_st) == 0 || any(basename(bio_raw) %in% src_met_st)
      if (!has_par_st || !has_met_st) {
        miss <- c(if (!has_par_st) "parent", if (!has_met_st) "metabolite")
        cat("  WARNING: selected files lack confirmed", paste(miss, collapse=" + "),
            "— ratio not computable for this dataset\n")
      }
    } else {
      bio_raw      <- all_bio_raw
      an_with_conf <- names(an_meta)
      cat("  NOTE: no confirmed source_file — using all analyses\n")
    }

    bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]] <- an_with_conf
    bio_files_per_ds[[ds]]  <- bio_raw

    if (length(an_with_conf) > 1)
      cat("  NOTE: confirmed files span", length(an_with_conf),
          "analyses:", paste(an_with_conf, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }

  # ── Both-roles check (all dataset types) ─────────────────────────────────
  if (!is.null(bio_files_per_ds[[ds]])) {
    ds_roles <- unique(conf_final$role[conf_final$dataset_id == ds])
    if (!all(c("parent", "metabolite") %in% ds_roles))
      cat("  WARNING: only role(s) [", paste(ds_roles, collapse=", "),
          "] confirmed — ratio not computable\n")
  }

  n_files <- if (is.list(bio_files_per_ds[[ds]]) && !is.character(bio_files_per_ds[[ds]]))
               sum(sapply(bio_files_per_ds[[ds]], length))
             else
               length(bio_files_per_ds[[ds]])
  cat("  →", n_files, "biological files |",
      length(bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]]), "assay(s)\n")
}
```

```{r bio-file-counts}
# Summary table: biological files + assay fractionation per confirmed dataset.
# Datasets where n_assays > 1 will need separate Spectra objects and
# separate RT/mz windows when scaling to all confirmed datasets.
bio_counts <- data.frame(
  dataset_id  = names(bio_files_per_ds),
  n_bio_files = sapply(bio_files_per_ds, function(x) {
    if (is.list(x) && !is.character(x)) sum(sapply(x, length)) else length(x)
  }),
  n_assays    = sapply(names(bio_files_per_ds), function(ds) {
    length(bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]])
  }),
  multi_assay = sapply(names(bio_files_per_ds), function(ds) {
    length(bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]]) > 1
  }),
  assay_ids   = sapply(names(bio_files_per_ds), function(ds) {
    paste(basename(bio_assays_per_ds[[ds]]), collapse = "; ")
  }),
  row.names = NULL
)
bio_counts <- dplyr::left_join(bio_counts,
  ds_summary[, c("dataset_id", "repository", "matrix", "n_subjects")],
  by = "dataset_id")
bio_counts
```

# Single-dataset prototype — MTBLS1866

MTBLS1866 is the cleanest candidate: Q Exactive Plus, RP-C18, DDA,
5-group COVID severity design, both parent and 5-OH metabolite confirmed
at strict / standard. We walk through the full EIC → peak detection
pipeline on a 10-sample subset, then decide on filtering rules before
scaling to all confirmed datasets.

### m/z and RT window strategy

**m/z:** We use the **median observed precursor m/z** of the confirmed
SIRIUS features for this dataset (stored in `conf_final$mz`, extracted
from the actual MS2 scan headers during confirmation). We do not use
the theoretical mass. Reasons:

1. The instrument's mass accuracy may be systematically shifted (e.g.,
   a few ppm offset due to recalibration). The observed m/z absorbs
   this shift automatically.
2. Different adducts ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, ...) give very different m/z
   values. Using the observed m/z means the EIC window is anchored to
   whichever adduct SIRIUS confirmed, without having to hard-code adduct
   logic here.
3. Only adducts present in both roles are retained (see shared-adducts
   rule above), so the m/z we extract here is guaranteed to be
   chemically consistent across parent and metabolite.

**RT window:** Confirmed RT ± `RT_TOL_S` seconds. The tolerance is set
conservatively (30 s) to account for run-to-run gradient drift within
the same study. It can be tightened if multiple peaks appear within the
window.

```{r proto-config}
dataset_proto <- "MTBLS1866"
PPM       <- 20
RT_TOL_S  <- 30          # ± seconds around the confirmed RT window

proto_conf_all <- conf_final[conf_final$dataset_id == dataset_proto, ]

# --- Resolve a single assay for the prototype --------------------------
# Multi-assay studies host several assays per dataset (e.g. LC-MS positive
# / LC-MS negative / GCxGC-MS); each carries its own RT and m/z space.
# The prototype runs on ONE assay — pick the one with the most confirmed
# features that still has BOTH parent and metabolite present.
assay_tab <- proto_conf_all |>
  dplyr::group_by(assay) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_par = sum(role == "parent"),
    n_met = sum(role == "metabolite"),
    n_tot = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n_par > 0 & n_met > 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_tot))
if (!nrow(assay_tab))
  stop("No assay in ", dataset_proto, " has both parent and metabolite confirmed")
assay_proto <- assay_tab$assay[1]
cat("Available assays for", dataset_proto, ":\n"); print(assay_tab)
cat("Selected prototype assay:", assay_proto, "\n\n")

proto_conf <- proto_conf_all[proto_conf_all$assay == assay_proto, ]

# --- m/z anchor from the observed precursor m/z of confirmed features ---
# IMPORTANT: do NOT average across adducts. [M+H]+ (~346.12) and [M+Na]+
# (~368.10) for omeprazole sit ~22 Da apart; taking a median across them
# lands between two real peaks and points the EIC at empty space. We
# therefore pick the dominant adduct per role (most confirmed features)
# and median the observed m/z only within that adduct.
#
# conf_final$mz comes from precursorMz() of the matched MS2 scan in the
# confirmation step. The within-adduct median absorbs scan-level drift
# without crossing chemistry.
dominant_adduct <- function(df) {
  tab <- table(df$adduct_inferred[!is.na(df$adduct_inferred)])
  if (!length(tab)) return(NA_character_)
  names(tab)[which.max(tab)]
}

ADDUCT_PARENT <- dominant_adduct(proto_conf[proto_conf$role == "parent",     ])
ADDUCT_METAB  <- dominant_adduct(proto_conf[proto_conf$role == "metabolite", ])

MZ_PARENT <- median(
  proto_conf$mz[proto_conf$role == "parent" &
                proto_conf$adduct_inferred == ADDUCT_PARENT],
  na.rm = TRUE)
MZ_METAB  <- median(
  proto_conf$mz[proto_conf$role == "metabolite" &
                proto_conf$adduct_inferred == ADDUCT_METAB],
  na.rm = TRUE)

# Warn loudly if more than one adduct is present per role — we will only
# extract one m/z window; the other adduct's features are dropped.
all_par_adducts <- unique(proto_conf$adduct_inferred[proto_conf$role == "parent"])
all_met_adducts <- unique(proto_conf$adduct_inferred[proto_conf$role == "metabolite"])
if (length(setdiff(all_par_adducts, NA)) > 1)
  cat("NOTE: parent has multiple adducts —", paste(all_par_adducts, collapse=", "),
      "— EIC will use only", ADDUCT_PARENT, "\n")
if (length(setdiff(all_met_adducts, NA)) > 1)
  cat("NOTE: metabolite has multiple adducts —", paste(all_met_adducts, collapse=", "),
      "— EIC will use only", ADDUCT_METAB, "\n")

# --- RT window from the confirmation step (already in seconds) ---
# Restrict to the same adduct as the m/z anchor — different adducts can
# elute at the same time, but mixing their RTs into the window is still
# noisy when one adduct dominates.
rt_par <- range(proto_conf$rt[proto_conf$role == "parent" &
                              proto_conf$adduct_inferred == ADDUCT_PARENT],
                na.rm = TRUE)
rt_met <- range(proto_conf$rt[proto_conf$role == "metabolite" &
                              proto_conf$adduct_inferred == ADDUCT_METAB],
                na.rm = TRUE)
rt_par_win <- rt_par + c(-RT_TOL_S, RT_TOL_S)
rt_met_win <- rt_met + c(-RT_TOL_S, RT_TOL_S)

cat("parent     adduct =", ADDUCT_PARENT,
    "| mz =", round(MZ_PARENT, 5), "\n")
cat("metabolite adduct =", ADDUCT_METAB,
    "| mz =", round(MZ_METAB,  5), "\n")
cat("parent     mz window:", MZ_PARENT * (1 + PPM*1e-6 * c(-1, 1)), "\n")
cat("metabolite mz window:", MZ_METAB  * (1 + PPM*1e-6 * c(-1, 1)), "\n")
cat("parent     rt window:", round(rt_par_win, 1), "s\n")
cat("metabolite rt window:", round(rt_met_win, 1), "s\n")
cat("\nMASST hit source files used for confirmation (selected assay only):\n")
print(unique(proto_conf[, c("role", "xcms_fts", "confidence", "rt", "mz",
                             "adduct_inferred", "source_file")]))
```

## Stage 2a — pick 10 biological files

File selection comes from the metadata-based `bio_files_per_ds` built in the
section above — no filename heuristics, no need to download first.

```{r proto-file-list}
# bio_files_per_ds[[ds]] is a flat character vector for single-assay datasets
# and a named list (keyed by assay file name) for multi-assay datasets.
# Use the assay resolved in proto-config (assay_proto) to pull the exact
# file list for that assay — no name-pattern heuristics.
tmp_bio <- bio_files_per_ds[[dataset_proto]]
if (is.list(tmp_bio) && !is.character(tmp_bio)) {
  if (assay_proto %in% names(tmp_bio)) {
    cat("Multi-assay study: selecting assay '", assay_proto,
        "' (resolved from confirmed source files)\n", sep = "")
    all_bio <- tmp_bio[[assay_proto]]
  } else {
    cat("WARNING: assay_proto '", assay_proto,
        "' not in bio_files_per_ds — falling back to union of all assays\n",
        sep = "")
    all_bio <- unlist(tmp_bio, use.names = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  all_bio <- tmp_bio
}

# MsBackendMetaboLights expects bare filenames (no path prefix).
# The assay table stores full relative paths like FILES/DERIVED_FILES/pos/B-107.mzXML;
# mtbls_sync_data_files and backendInitialize both take basename only.
all_bio <- basename(all_bio)

cat("Biological files available for", dataset_proto, "/", assay_proto, ":",
    length(all_bio), "\n")

# --- Confirmed source files (positive-control "test" files) -------------
# These are the files where SIRIUS actually matched parent and/or metabolite
# in this assay. We add them on top of the random 10-sample subset so that
# (a) we can verify our EIC/peak-detection settings find signal where
#     SIRIUS already saw it, and
# (b) the random subset itself stays unbiased (10 truly random samples,
#     plus N test files appended).
test_files_proto <- unique(basename(
  proto_conf$source_file[!is.na(proto_conf$source_file)]))
test_files_proto <- test_files_proto[test_files_proto %in% all_bio]
cat("Confirmed test files in this assay:", length(test_files_proto), "\n")
if (length(test_files_proto)) print(test_files_proto)

# --- Random 10-sample subset, drawn from the REMAINING pool -------------
# Excluding test files from the random pool prevents double-counting and
# keeps the random draw representative of "unseen" samples.
random_pool <- setdiff(all_bio, test_files_proto)
set.seed(1)
random_files <- sample(random_pool, min(10, length(random_pool)))

proto_files <- unique(c(test_files_proto, random_files))
cat("Selected (", length(test_files_proto), "test +",
    length(random_files), "random =", length(proto_files), "files):\n", sep = " ")
print(proto_files)
```

## Stage 2b — sync and load (on disk)

```{r proto-sync-load}
mtbls_sync_data_files(mtblsId = dataset_proto, fileName = basename(proto_files))

sp <- Spectra(backendInitialize(
  MsBackendMetaboLights(),
  mtblsId = dataset_proto,
  fileName = basename(proto_files),
  offline = TRUE
))
ms1 <- filterMsLevel(sp, 1L)

cat("Files loaded :", length(unique(dataOrigin(ms1))), "\n")
cat("MS1 spectra  :", length(ms1), "\n")
```

## EIC extraction

We use `Chromatograms::chromExtract()` to extract EICs in a single pass
over the Spectra object. A *peak table* defines one extraction window per
(role × file): `rtMin`/`rtMax` from the confirmed-RT windows and
`mzMin`/`mzMax` from the target mass ± PPM tolerance. The `by` argument
tells `chromExtract` which peak-table columns to use as grouping keys when
matching spectra — here `msLevel` (MS1 only) and `dataOrigin` (one file per
row). The resulting `Chromatograms` object carries the full peak table as
`chromData()`, so subsetting by role is straightforward.

```{r proto-chromatograms, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
library(Chromatograms)

# One extraction window per role × file
all_orig <- unique(dataOrigin(ms1))

peak_tbl <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    role       = "parent",
    msLevel    = 1L,
    dataOrigin = all_orig,
    rtMin      = rt_par_win[1],  rtMax = rt_par_win[2],
    mzMin      = MZ_PARENT * (1 - PPM * 1e-6),
    mzMax      = MZ_PARENT * (1 + PPM * 1e-6),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    role       = "metabolite",
    msLevel    = 1L,
    dataOrigin = all_orig,
    rtMin      = rt_met_win[1],  rtMax = rt_met_win[2],
    mzMin      = MZ_METAB * (1 - PPM * 1e-6),
    mzMax      = MZ_METAB * (1 + PPM * 1e-6),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
)

chr_all  <- Chromatograms(ms1)
chr_eics <- chromExtract(chr_all, peak_tbl, by = c("msLevel", "dataOrigin"))

chr_par  <- chr_eics[chromData(chr_eics)$role == "parent"]
chr_met  <- chr_eics[chromData(chr_eics)$role == "metabolite"]

# plotChromatogramsOverlay sets ylim from the first chromatogram it draws,
# so any file with higher intensity gets clipped.  Pre-compute ylim across
# all EICs for each role and pass it explicitly.
eic_ylim <- function(chr) {
  ints <- unlist(lapply(peaksData(chr), `[[`, "intensity"), use.names = FALSE)
  c(0, max(ints, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05)   # 5 % headroom
}

# Call with package qualifier — xcms masks plotChromatogramsOverlay
par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4, 2, 1))
Chromatograms::plotChromatogramsOverlay(
  chr_par,
  main = paste(dataset_proto, "— omeprazole (parent)"),
  ylim = eic_ylim(chr_par))
Chromatograms::plotChromatogramsOverlay(
  chr_met,
  main = paste(dataset_proto, "— 5-OH-omeprazole (metabolite)"),
  ylim = eic_ylim(chr_met))
```

## Peak detection

`MsCoreUtils::localMaxima` is applied to the full intensity vector
(including NAs; the C code never returns NA positions as maxima).
`hws` sets the half-window in scans; a peak must be the maximum within
±`hws` neighbours. RT and AUC are computed separately via MsQuality.

```{r proto-peaks}
count_peaks <- function(chr, hws = 3L, pct_max = 0.1) {
  ints <- intensity(chr)
  vapply(ints, function(x) {
    mx <- max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (!is.finite(mx)) return(0L)
    x_s <- x[!is.na(x)]
    lm  <- MsCoreUtils::localMaxima(x_s, hws = hws)
    sum(lm & x_s >= pct_max * mx)
  }, integer(1L))
}

peaks_par <- count_peaks(chr_par)
peaks_met <- count_peaks(chr_met)

cat("Parent     — files with ≥1 peak:", sum(peaks_par > 1), "/",
    length(peaks_par), "\n")
cat("Metabolite — files with ≥1 peak:", sum(peaks_met > 1), "/",
    length(peaks_met), "\n")
```

Here check that we have not more than one peak.
For now, on the small subset it looks great. and the sanity check look very  good.
I would do another check on the full dataset before we go on to all the data.


## Positive-control check

SIRIUS-confirmed files are positive controls: our EIC pipeline must
detect a peak there. Failures flag a settings problem (PPM, RT window,
or adduct choice). We run this check BEFORE dropping empty EICs so we
notice if a confirmed file would be silently discarded.

```{r proto-verify-signal}
conf_par_files <- unique(basename(proto_conf$source_file[
  proto_conf$role == "parent" & !is.na(proto_conf$source_file)]))
conf_met_files <- unique(basename(proto_conf$source_file[
  proto_conf$role == "metabolite" & !is.na(proto_conf$source_file)]))

par_files_all <- basename(chromData(chr_par)[["dataOrigin"]])
met_files_all <- basename(chromData(chr_met)[["dataOrigin"]])

check_confirmed <- function(files, n_peaks, conf_files, role) {
  idx <- which(files %in% conf_files)
  cat(role, "— confirmed files loaded:", length(idx),
      "| with >=1 peak:", sum(n_peaks[idx] > 0), "\n")
  missed <- files[idx[n_peaks[idx] == 0]]
  if (length(missed)) cat("  WARNING missed:", paste(missed, collapse=", "), "\n")
}

check_confirmed(par_files_all, peaks_par, conf_par_files, "Parent    ")
check_confirmed(met_files_all, peaks_met, conf_met_files, "Metabolite")
```

## Drop empty EICs

A chromatogram with zero detected peaks carries no usable signal — its
trapezoidal integral is just baseline drift, and `peakBoundary()` has
nothing to anchor to. We drop empty EICs per-role (NOT per-file) so
asymmetric cases (parent visible / metabolite not, or vice versa) are
still represented in the sample table; the *file* survives even though
one of its two EICs has been dropped.

```{r proto-drop-empty}
keep_par <- peaks_par > 0
keep_met <- peaks_met > 0

chr_par_ok <- chr_par[keep_par]
chr_met_ok <- chr_met[keep_met]

cat("Parent     EICs kept :", sum(keep_par), "/", length(keep_par),
    " (dropped:", sum(!keep_par), ")\n")
cat("Metabolite EICs kept :", sum(keep_met), "/", length(keep_met),
    " (dropped:", sum(!keep_met), ")\n")

# Track which files retain each role — used by the sample table to
# assign a detection tier (both / parent_only / metab_only / neither).
files_par_ok <- basename(chromData(chr_par_ok)[["dataOrigin"]])
files_met_ok <- basename(chromData(chr_met_ok)[["dataOrigin"]])
```

## Peak boundaries and narrow re-extraction

`Chromatograms::peakBoundary()` returns the rtime boundaries of the
dominant peak per EIC, derived from a baseline-quantile threshold. We
re-extract a narrower EIC over `[left_boundary - PAD, right_boundary +
PAD]` from the original `chr_all` Spectra so trapezoidal AUC and FWHM
are computed strictly on the peak region — not on the broad RT window
we used for detection. The small PAD captures the tails the
baseline-cut clips.

```{r proto-peakbounds}
BOUND_PAD_S <- 5  # seconds of padding on each side of the boundary

# Re-extract narrow EICs.  We feed peakBoundary back into chromExtract
# via a fresh peak_tbl so the result has the same `dataOrigin` ordering
# as the input — important for downstream joins.
narrow_extract <- function(chr, role, mz_centre, ppm) {
  bnd <- Chromatograms::peakBoundary(chr)            # n x 2 matrix
  cd  <- chromData(chr)
  ok  <- is.finite(bnd[, "left_boundary"]) &
         is.finite(bnd[, "right_boundary"])
  if (!any(ok)) return(chr[FALSE])
  pt  <- data.frame(
    role       = role,
    msLevel    = 1L,
    dataOrigin = cd[["dataOrigin"]][ok],
    rtMin      = bnd[ok, "left_boundary"]  - BOUND_PAD_S,
    rtMax      = bnd[ok, "right_boundary"] + BOUND_PAD_S,
    mzMin      = mz_centre * (1 - ppm * 1e-6),
    mzMax      = mz_centre * (1 + ppm * 1e-6),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  chromExtract(chr_all, pt, by = c("msLevel", "dataOrigin"))
}

chr_par_narrow <- narrow_extract(chr_par_ok, "parent",     MZ_PARENT, PPM)
chr_met_narrow <- narrow_extract(chr_met_ok, "metabolite", MZ_METAB,  PPM)

cat("Narrow EICs — parent:", length(chr_par_narrow),
    "| metabolite:", length(chr_met_narrow), "\n")
```

## EIC metrics via MsQuality

`MsQuality::calculateMetrics()` is the high-level dispatcher: it
inspects the class of `object` and forwards to the right backend
(`calculateMetricsFromChromatograms()` for our `Chromatograms` input,
`…FromSpectra` for raw spectra, `…FromMsExperiment` for full
experiments). Using the dispatcher keeps this chunk class-agnostic —
if we later switch to processing `MsExperiment` objects, the call
doesn't change. It returns one row per `dataOrigin` with columns named
after the requested metrics. We pull the integrated area
(`areaUnderTic`), the chromatographic peak width at half-max
(`xicFwhm`, computed internally from a fresh `peakBoundary`), the apex
prominence (`peakProminence`), and the raw `peakWidth` (RT range
covered by data) for diagnostics. The `peakCount` metric here counts
*MS scans*, not chromatographic peaks — we already established those
above with the local-maxima detector.

```{r proto-msquality}
library(MsQuality)

EIC_METRICS <- c("areaUnderTic", "xicFwhm", "peakProminence", "peakWidth")

tidy_metrics <- function(chr, prefix) {
  if (!length(chr))
    return(data.frame(file = character(0)))
  m <- calculateMetrics(chr, metrics = EIC_METRICS, msLevel = 1L)
  data.frame(
    file       = basename(rownames(m)),
    auc        = m[["areaUnderTic"]],
    fwhm       = m[["xicFwhm"]],
    prominence = m[["peakProminence"]],
    pkwidth    = m[["peakWidth"]],
    row.names  = NULL,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    setNames(c("file", paste0(prefix, "_",
                              c("auc","fwhm","prominence","pkwidth"))))
}

metrics_par <- tidy_metrics(chr_par_narrow, "par")
metrics_met <- tidy_metrics(chr_met_narrow, "met")

metrics_par
metrics_met
```

## FWHM outlier check

Within the same dataset the chromatographic peak width should be
roughly constant — the gradient is fixed, the same compound elutes the
same way across injections. A file whose FWHM departs strongly from
the median (here: > 3 × MAD) usually means the EIC is integrating two
fused peaks, baseline noise, or a co-eluting isobar — i.e., the AUC
for that file is suspect and should be flagged before it enters the
ratio.

```{r proto-fwhm-outliers}
flag_fwhm <- function(df, col) {
  v   <- df[[col]]
  med <- median(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  mad <- stats::mad(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(mad) || mad == 0)
    return(rep(FALSE, length(v)))
  abs(v - med) > 3 * mad
}

metrics_par$par_fwhm_outlier <- flag_fwhm(metrics_par, "par_fwhm")
metrics_met$met_fwhm_outlier <- flag_fwhm(metrics_met, "met_fwhm")

cat("Parent     FWHM (s): median =",
    round(median(metrics_par$par_fwhm, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    "| outliers (>3 MAD):", sum(metrics_par$par_fwhm_outlier), "\n")
cat("Metabolite FWHM (s): median =",
    round(median(metrics_met$met_fwhm, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    "| outliers (>3 MAD):", sum(metrics_met$met_fwhm_outlier), "\n")
```

### Visualise the flagged peaks

Plot each FWHM-outlier EIC alongside a reference EIC drawn from the
file closest to the median FWHM. A genuine outlier will look obviously
deformed against the reference — double apex, asymmetric tail, broad
shoulder, or noisy baseline. If the outlier looks structurally similar
to the reference, the flag is a false alarm (typically driven by a
small absolute FWHM in a dataset with low FWHM variance) and the file
should stay in the ratio.

```{r proto-fwhm-outliers-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
plot_fwhm_outliers <- function(chr, metrics, prefix, role_label) {
  oc <- paste0(prefix, "_fwhm_outlier")
  fc <- paste0(prefix, "_fwhm")
  out_files <- metrics$file[metrics[[oc]] %in% TRUE]
  if (!length(out_files) || !length(chr)) {
    cat("No FWHM outliers for ", role_label, " — nothing to plot.\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  files_chr <- basename(chromData(chr)[["dataOrigin"]])
  med_fwhm  <- median(metrics[[fc]], na.rm = TRUE)
  ref_file  <- metrics$file[which.min(abs(metrics[[fc]] - med_fwhm))]
  to_show   <- unique(c(ref_file, out_files))

  rows <- lapply(seq_along(files_chr), function(i) {
    f <- files_chr[i]
    if (!(f %in% to_show)) return(NULL)
    pd <- peaksData(chr)[[i]]
    fwhm_v <- metrics[[fc]][match(f, metrics$file)]
    data.frame(
      file      = f,
      rtime     = pd$rtime,
      intensity = pd$intensity,
      panel     = paste0(f, "\nFWHM = ", round(fwhm_v, 1), " s"),
      kind      = ifelse(f == ref_file,
                         "reference (median FWHM)", "outlier"),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  # Stable panel order: reference first, then outliers sorted by FWHM
  fwhm_lookup <- setNames(metrics[[fc]], metrics$file)
  df$panel <- factor(df$panel,
    levels = unique(df$panel[order(df$file != ref_file,
                                   fwhm_lookup[df$file])]))

  ggplot(df, aes(rtime, intensity, colour = kind)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("reference (median FWHM)" = "grey40",
                 "outlier"                  = "#D7191C")) +
    labs(title    = paste(dataset_proto, "—", role_label, "FWHM outliers"),
         subtitle = paste0("Median FWHM = ", round(med_fwhm, 1),
                           " s | outlier rule: |FWHM - median| > 3 * MAD"),
         x = "Retention time (s)", y = "Intensity", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = 8))
}

plot_fwhm_outliers(chr_par_narrow, metrics_par, "par", "parent")
plot_fwhm_outliers(chr_met_narrow, metrics_met, "met", "metabolite")
```

## Canonical metadata resolution

Three sources contribute per-file metadata, with a fixed priority:

1. **Repository per-sample file** (`s_*.txt` for MetaboLights,
   `*_metadata.tsv` for MassIVE/Pan-ReDU, `SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS` in
   mwtab files for Metabolomics Workbench). Read once per dataset, joined
   to file basenames via the assay table's `Sample Name → Derived
   Spectral Data File` map.
2. **`dataset_curation_table.csv`** — the human-readable curation
   notebook. Names the raw column per canonical field with coverage
   tags (`"Yes - Comment[Patient status] (100%)"`) and stores
   per-dataset constants (`country = "Italy (Novara University
   Hospital, …)"` for MTBLS1866, taken from the paper).
3. **Linked paper** — only where the deposit is silent. For MTBLS1866
   the paper (Barberis et al. 2020, PMC7696386) supplies `country` as
   a per-dataset constant, and gives per-arm aggregates for sex and
   age (Table 1) that are NOT mappable to individual files.

Each canonical field is therefore one of three granularities:

| granularity              | example field      | how it lands in `meta`            |
|--------------------------|--------------------|------------------------------------|
| per-file                 | `health_status`    | row-level join from the s-file     |
| per-dataset constant     | `country`          | broadcast scalar from curation     |
| per-group aggregate only | `sex`, `age`       | NA at per-file level; summarised separately |

A **`subject_id`** is also tracked per file. For MTBLS1866 the
deposit is 1:1 (`Source Name == Sample Name`, no replicates), so it
collapses trivially. For datasets with technical replicate injections
or multi-timepoint sampling, this column is what we will deduplicate
on before stats — counting one subject once, not once per injection.

```{r resolve-metadata}
# This block is hard-wired to the prototype (MTBLS1866); the
# all-datasets pass turns it into a function that branches on dataset_id
# prefix and reads the curation row's column-name strings.

curation_row <- curation[curation$dataset_id == dataset_proto, ]

s_tbl <- read.delim(
  file.path("dataset_metadata", paste0("s_", dataset_proto, ".txt")),
  check.names = FALSE)
a_tbl <- read.delim(
  file.path("dataset_metadata", assay_proto),
  check.names = FALSE)

# file basename -> Sample Name via assay's Derived Spectral Data File
file_to_sample <- setNames(
  a_tbl[["Sample Name"]],
  basename(a_tbl[["Derived Spectral Data File"]]))

meta <- data.frame(
  file       = proto_files,
  subject_id = unname(file_to_sample[proto_files]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Per-file from repo s-file (MTBLS1866-specific column names — in the
# generalised version, parse `curation_row$health_status` for the
# bracketed column name)
sidx <- match(meta$subject_id, s_tbl[["Sample Name"]])
meta$health_status <- s_tbl[["Comment[Patient status]"]][sidx]
meta$body_site     <- s_tbl[["Characteristics[Organism part]"]][sidx]

# Per-dataset constant from curation/paper
meta$country       <- "Italy"   # Barberis 2020 — Novara University Hospital

# Not mappable per file for this deposit (paper Table 1 is per-arm only)
meta$sex           <- NA_character_
meta$age           <- NA_real_

cat("Canonical metadata for", dataset_proto, "(", nrow(meta), "files):\n")
cat("  subject_id    : ", length(unique(meta$subject_id)),
    "unique subjects (", nrow(meta), "files = ",
    round(nrow(meta)/length(unique(meta$subject_id)),1), "files/subject)\n")
cat("  health_status : filled =", sum(!is.na(meta$health_status)),
    "/", nrow(meta), "\n")
cat("  body_site     : filled =", sum(!is.na(meta$body_site)), "/", nrow(meta), "\n")
cat("  country       : filled =", sum(!is.na(meta$country)),
    "/", nrow(meta), "  (constant from paper)\n")
cat("  sex / age     : NA per file (paper Table 1 is per-arm aggregate only)\n\n")
print(meta)
```

## Sample table — detection tiers

A sample's *detection tier* records which roles produced a peak:

| tier         | parent peak | metabolite peak | ratio computable                       |
|--------------|-------------|-----------------|----------------------------------------|
| `both`       | yes         | yes             | yes — `log2(par/met)`                  |
| `parent_only`| yes         | no              | no — censored high (low CYP2C19)       |
| `metab_only` | no          | yes             | no — censored low (high CYP2C19)       |
| `neither`    | no          | no              | sample contributes nothing             |

The ratio is computed *only* for `both`. Asymmetric cases stay in the
table as categorical readouts — we do not impute the missing AUC and we
do not set the ratio to 1 (which would imply equal amounts, the wrong
conclusion).

```{r sample-table}
# Outer-join the two metric tables so files in only one role survive.
sample_tbl <- merge(metrics_par, metrics_met, by = "file", all = TRUE)
sample_tbl <- merge(data.frame(file = proto_files), sample_tbl,
                    by = "file", all.x = TRUE)
sample_tbl <- merge(sample_tbl, meta, by = "file", all.x = TRUE)

sample_tbl$detection_tier <- with(sample_tbl, ifelse(
  !is.na(par_auc) & !is.na(met_auc), "both",
  ifelse(!is.na(par_auc) & is.na(met_auc), "parent_only",
  ifelse( is.na(par_auc) & !is.na(met_auc), "metab_only",
                                            "neither"))))

# Ratio only where both detected
sample_tbl$log2_ratio <- with(sample_tbl, ifelse(
  detection_tier == "both", log2(par_auc / met_auc), NA_real_))

# Subject-level deduplication: if a subject contributed multiple
# injections (not the case for MTBLS1866, but routine elsewhere), keep
# the row with the highest summed AUC so a single subject contributes a
# single ratio.  For 1:1 datasets this is a no-op.
n_before <- nrow(sample_tbl)
sample_tbl <- sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::group_by(subject_id) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(
    order_by = dplyr::coalesce(par_auc, 0) + dplyr::coalesce(met_auc, 0),
    n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
n_after <- nrow(sample_tbl)
if (n_before != n_after)
  cat("Subject-level dedup: collapsed", n_before, "->", n_after,
      "(replicates per subject:",
      round(n_before / length(unique(sample_tbl$subject_id)), 2), ")\n")

cat("Detection tier counts:\n"); print(table(sample_tbl$detection_tier))
sample_tbl
```

## Ratio handling — the parent-only file

In this prototype run we have at least one file with parent detected
but no metabolite. Biologically, for CYP2C19 phenotyping, that profile
is **informative**: it points to a poor metabolizer (the substrate is
present, the enzyme is not turning it over). Three options for scoring
it:

1. **Drop the sample.** Loses real signal — poor metabolizers are
   exactly the phenotype we want to detect.
2. **Set ratio = 1.** Wrong: implies parent ≈ metabolite, which is the
   profile of an *extensive* metabolizer. This would invert the
   biological meaning.
3. **Treat as right-censored.** Keep the sample, note `detection_tier
   == "parent_only"`, and in the stats stage use either (a) a
   detection-status logistic test (parent_only count vs both count per
   group) or (b) impute `met_auc` to the per-dataset noise floor (e.g.
   half the smallest detected `met_auc`) and label the resulting ratio
   as a lower bound.

The prototype uses option 3a: the ratio stays NA for `parent_only` and
the file enters the categorical analysis. We revisit imputation when
scaling to all datasets, because the noise floor is dataset-specific.

```{r stats}
both <- sample_tbl[sample_tbl$detection_tier == "both" &
                   !sample_tbl$par_fwhm_outlier %in% TRUE &
                   !sample_tbl$met_fwhm_outlier %in% TRUE, ]

cat("Samples entering ratio stats:", nrow(both),
    " | parent_only (censored):",
    sum(sample_tbl$detection_tier == "parent_only"),
    " | metab_only:",
    sum(sample_tbl$detection_tier == "metab_only"),
    " | neither:",
    sum(sample_tbl$detection_tier == "neither"), "\n")

# wilcox.test(log2_ratio ~ HealthStatus, data = both)   # enable when metadata joined
```

## Plots

```{r plots}
# log2 ratio distribution (only `both` samples).  Censored cases
# (parent_only / metab_only) are shown as a side panel count for context
# — they don't have a numeric ratio.
ggplot(both, aes(x = "samples", y = log2_ratio)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log2(omeprazole / 5-OH-omeprazole)",
       title = paste0(dataset_proto, " — ratio distribution (n=", nrow(both), ")"),
       subtitle = paste0("Censored: parent_only=",
                         sum(sample_tbl$detection_tier == "parent_only"),
                         ", metab_only=",
                         sum(sample_tbl$detection_tier == "metab_only"))) +
  theme_bw()

# Parent vs metabolite area, with detection tier as colour so the
# censored cases are visible on the axes (along x=NA or y=NA strip).
ggplot(sample_tbl,
       aes(par_auc, met_auc, colour = detection_tier,
           shape = par_fwhm_outlier | met_fwhm_outlier)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.85, size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 4),
                     name = "FWHM outlier") +
  labs(x = "omeprazole area", y = "5-OH-omeprazole area",
       colour = "Detection tier", title = dataset_proto) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Metadata limitations and unsupervised exploration

What we resolved per file for MTBLS1866 is the rule, not the
exception. Across the tier-B curated datasets, only a minority
of public deposits ship the biological covariates (sex, age, country,
treatment, BMI, ethnicity) that a phenotyping analysis would normally
adjust for. The MASST/Pan-ReDU `ATTRIBUTE_*` columns are usable when
the depositor populated them but are empty for most MetaboLights and
Metabolomics Workbench studies, and the linked papers — when they
exist — typically report demographics as per-arm aggregates (Table 1
sex/age) rather than as per-sample tables joinable to file names.

For our analysis this has two concrete consequences:

1. **Unadjustable confounding.** A ratio difference we observe between
   two datasets could reflect a real biological effect or simply
   a difference in sex / age / ancestry composition that we cannot
   model. Within-dataset contrasts (e.g. the 5-level COVID severity
   here) are insulated from this; cross-dataset meta-analysis is not.
2. **Limited stratification.** Within most deposits the only available
   stratifier is the study's primary design factor (case vs control,
   severity grade, …). Secondary effects we would normally investigate
   — e.g. is the CYP2C19 ratio sex-dependent in this cohort? — are not
   testable from the public data alone.

## Unsupervised structure as a metadata-gap diagnostic

A practical workaround is to run an unsupervised analysis on the
per-file metric matrix (`par_auc`, `met_auc`, `par_fwhm`, `met_fwhm`,
`log2_ratio`) and check whether the resulting structure aligns with
the *available* metadata. If a clear cluster split emerges that does
**not** track `health_status` (the only per-file factor we have), that
split is evidence of a latent covariate the deposit does not expose —
which is itself a finding worth reporting. The unsupervised view
becomes a missing-metadata diagnostic, not just an exploratory plot.

```{r unsup-pca, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
# PCA over the per-file metric matrix, restricted to the `both` tier
# (numeric ratio available). Need at least 5 samples and at least 2
# non-constant columns to be meaningful.
#
# Implementation notes:
#   - sample_tbl is a tibble (dplyr pipeline above). as.matrix() on a
#     tibble drops row names, so we cannot rely on rownames(pc$x) to map
#     PC rows back to metadata.  We add an explicit `.row_id` column,
#     copy it into rownames(pc_mat), and read it back as integer.
#   - complete.cases() before prcomp is required: scale. = TRUE divides
#     by per-column sd, which is NaN if any NA is present.

both_for_pca <- as.data.frame(
  sample_tbl[sample_tbl$detection_tier == "both", ])
both_for_pca$.row_id <- seq_len(nrow(both_for_pca))

pc_cols <- c("par_auc","met_auc","par_fwhm","met_fwhm","log2_ratio")
pc_mat  <- as.matrix(both_for_pca[, pc_cols])
rownames(pc_mat) <- as.character(both_for_pca$.row_id)

# Keep non-constant columns
inf_cols <- apply(pc_mat, 2, function(x) {
  v <- stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE); !is.na(v) && v > 0 })
pc_mat <- pc_mat[, inf_cols, drop = FALSE]

# Drop rows with any NA across the kept columns
pc_mat <- pc_mat[stats::complete.cases(pc_mat), , drop = FALSE]

if (nrow(pc_mat) >= 5 && ncol(pc_mat) >= 2) {
  pc      <- stats::prcomp(pc_mat, scale. = TRUE)
  row_ids <- as.integer(rownames(pc$x))         # safely tracked
  pc_df   <- cbind(
    as.data.frame(pc$x[, 1:min(2, ncol(pc$x)), drop = FALSE]),
    both_for_pca[row_ids,
                 c("subject_id","health_status","country"),
                 drop = FALSE])

  ggplot(pc_df, aes(PC1, PC2,
                    colour = health_status,
                    label  = subject_id)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_text(vjust = -0.7, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    labs(title    = paste(dataset_proto, "— PCA of EIC metrics"),
         subtitle = "Cluster splits not tracking health_status hint at unmeasured covariates",
         caption  = paste("n =", nrow(pc_df), "subjects | available factors:",
                          "health_status, body_site, country (constant)")) +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
} else {
  cat("Skipping PCA — need >=5 `both` samples and >=2 non-constant metrics",
      "(have", nrow(pc_mat), "rows,", ncol(pc_mat), "informative cols)\n")
}
```

## A note for the paper

The same diagnostic, run dataset by dataset, becomes a quantitative
argument for richer mandatory metadata in public metabolomics
repositories: how many datasets show unsupervised structure that the
available metadata cannot explain? A handful would already justify
proposing a minimum-metadata standard (at least `BiologicalSex`,
`AgeInYears`, `Country`, and a structured `treatment_history` field
where ethical) at the level of MetaboLights / Workbench submission
templates and Pan-ReDU re-annotation. This finding is a free side
benefit of the pipeline — we get it from the same metric matrix that
feeds the ratio analysis, no extra computation.

# Sanity check

Does the result match the pharmacology literature? For this compound
pair, CYP2C19-extensive metabolisers show a lower parent/5-OH ratio
than poor metabolisers. If the prototype dataset is not CYP2C19-
stratified or PPI-intervention designed, re-select `dataset_proto`.
